problem: A mobile railway platform has a horizontal bottom in the form of a rectangle 10 meters long and 4 meters wide, loaded with sand. The surface of the sand has an angle of no more than 45 degrees with the base plane (otherwise the sand grains will spill), the density of the sand is 1500 kg/m³. Find the maximum mass of sand loaded onto the platform.

answer_text:
# Maximum Mass of Sand on a Railway Platform

## Setting Up the Geometry

To maximize the amount of sand on the 10 m × 4 m platform while keeping the surface slope at or below 45°, the sand forms a **triangular prism** (wedge) with:
- A **ridge running along the 10 m length** (the longer dimension)
- Two sloping faces making exactly 45° with the horizontal

## Finding the Height of the Sand Pile

The cross-section perpendicular to the ridge is an **isosceles triangle** with:
- Base = 4 m (the width of the platform)
- Each sloping side at 45° to the horizontal

Since each side covers half the base (2 m) horizontally:

$$\tan 45° = \frac{h}{2} \implies h = 2 \times 1 = 2 \text{ m}$$

## Computing the Volume

**Cross-sectional area:**
$$A = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 2 = 4 \text{ m}^2$$

**Volume of the triangular prism:**
$$V = A \times L = 4 \times 10 = 40 \text{ m}^3$$

## Computing the Mass

$$m = \rho \times V = 1500 \text{ kg/m}^3 \times 40 \text{ m}^3 = 60{,}000 \text{ kg}$$

## Verification of the Constraint

Each face rises 2 m over a horizontal run of 2 m, giving a slope angle of:
$$\theta = \arctan\!\left(\frac{2}{2}\right) = \arctan(1) = 45° \checkmark$$

This is exactly at the maximum allowed angle, confirming the volume is maximized.

$$\boxed{60000}$$
